clue.text: The best soft bed — this is suitable for singles

parts.note: a record is the best performance ever achieved
P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft
a bed of rock or soil is a layer

explanation.surface: An advert for the finest soft mattress, ideal for someone who sleeps alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singles' looks like single beds or single people, but it means short records played on a turntable.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is a short vinyl disc, and a turntable machine is what plays one.

clue.text: Sally swimming to piers

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally swims out to the piers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name, but here it means a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty reply, which is what a riposte is.

clue.text: Cable cut American soldier's dog

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a cord is a cable
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier's dog has chewed through a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final D of CORD to give COR.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Sarnie with no spread? Good thinking

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for leaving the butter out of a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like butter in the surface but signals the anagram of SARNIE NO, giving REASONIN. A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of thinking logically.

clue.text: Expression of relief from hardly any by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is said aloud and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: few means hardly any

explanation.surface: Someone barely relieved at all, judging by their tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is the exclamation people make when a worry passes.

clue.text: Tries picking up volunteers with invites

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to invite can mean to tempt or entice

explanation.surface: Recruiting attempts to collect volunteers by sending out invitations.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British Army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are tries, efforts at doing something.

clue.text: Precise demand

definitions.meaning: to ... as a verb is to demand

explanation.surface: A call for strict accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate as an adjective, and to insist upon payment as a verb.

clue.text: Mount most suitable horse, perhaps

parts.note: best means most suitable
a horse is an example of a ride

explanation.surface: Climb on the most suitable horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a noun meaning horse, but it is the verb for sitting astride.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to sit astride something, as one mounts a horse.

clue.text: Pretty, magical creature captivates student

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the creature's letters enclose the student

parts.note: a fairy is a magical creature
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A pretty fairy enchants a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective for the fairy, but means rather, an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and fairly are both adverbs meaning moderately, as in fairly good.

clue.text: Writer holding broken arm hospital department fixed

indicators.note: holding means the writer's letters go round the shuffled ones

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: something broken has its pieces rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A writer with a broken arm gets it set by the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken arm' and 'hospital' paint an injury, but 'broken' only signals the anagram and 'holding' the insertion; 'fixed' is the definition, not the bone being set.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed in place is lasting, which is what permanent means.

clue.text: Place enthralling Roman, ultimately?

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the place's letters hold the picked letter

parts.note: an area is a place or region

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Roman

explanation.surface: A venue that captivated the Romans in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the arena was the venue where Romans were held spellbound by games.
explanation.definitionFit: The amphitheatre where gladiators fought was the spectacle venue that gripped Roman crowds.

clue.text: Son and I journey inside an Asian city

indicators.note: inside means I and the journey word sit within the word an

parts.note: to go is to journey

explanation.surface: A father describes a trip he and his son are taking within Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon is the former name of Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam.

clue.text: Initially indicating bananas to a trim ape?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word indicating
bananas means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A hint that something goes crazy when a neat ape appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' also suits the ape of the surface, but it is the anagram signal: TO A TRIM rearranges to MITATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an ape is someone who copies others, a mimic.

clue.text: Former lover with old sign of nerves? That's unusual

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to find an ex-partner showing a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means strikingly strange or foreign, hence out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Heads containing sanctimonious thoughts

indicators.note: containing means the heads word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: onion is slang for head, so onions are heads
pi is a crossword staple for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Smug, self-righteous ideas in people's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onion' is old slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views or beliefs, what one thinks.

clue.text: Sadly tie knots at a constant rate

indicators.note: to knot is to tangle, so the letters are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone glumly tying knots, one after another at an even pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knots' looks like a noun in the surface but is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadily describes doing something evenly without speeding up or slowing down.

clue.text: A labyrinth intended to bring out adult's surprise

parts.note: a maze is a labyrinth

indicators.note: bringing something out means removing it from inside

parts.note: meant means intended
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: A maze designed to draw out a grown-up's sense of wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring out' removes the A from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is a feeling of great astonishment.

clue.text: Almost frighten one Conservative? Wicked!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to terrify is to frighten
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Tory nearly being scared, and someone cheering 'Wicked!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked!' is slang for excellent, not evil.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang both words are exclamations of approval meaning excellent.

clue.text: Squirms right after women's laughs? Not at first

indicators.note: after means the right letter follows the women letter

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: giggles are laughs

explanation.surface: Someone squirming, perhaps right after hearing women laughing at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' removes the opening G of GIGGLES, leaving IGGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm is to twist and wriggle about uncomfortably.

clue.text: Sensibly is supporting wife really regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the word is goes underneath
regularly picks every other letter of the word really

explanation.surface: A husband sensibly backing his wife at every turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of really, ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisely means with good judgement, i.e. sensibly.

clue.text: Approached 50 small animals

parts.note: to approach is to come near, so came
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Some fifty little animals drew near.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are humped desert beasts, an example of animals.

clue.text: Shots from England cricketer securing runs

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the cricketer's name goes round the other letter

parts.note: Ben Stokes is an England cricketer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting shots that bring in runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes is a star all-rounder and captain of England's cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: In sports like cricket, golf or tennis a stroke is a hit or shot.

clue.text: Footwear next to yard not to be trusted

parts.note: a slipper is a piece of footwear

explanation.surface: A shoe left by a yard of ground that cannot be relied upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery person is shifty and evasive, so unreliable.

clue.text: Church is after pound coins

indicators.note: is after means the church letters follow the pound word

parts.note: a pound is an animal enclosure, a pen
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church wanting a pound in small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money beside 'coins' but means a pen for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are the small coins of British currency, a hundred to the pound.

clue.text: Moderate fit of rage

explanation.surface: Advice to tone down an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Temper as a verb means to tone down; as a noun it is a bout of anger.

clue.text: Go topless in European river for picture

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a go is a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: Going topless in a European river for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun here, an attempt, not the verb of the surface; 'topless' drops its synonym's first letter and 'in' places the rest inside the Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Moira Stuart's turning up wearing long garment

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
wearing means the name carries the letters within it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The newsreader Moira Stuart appears dressed in a long robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'wearing long garment' as the definition, but a sari is not 'wearing' anything; 'wearing' signals the hidden IRAS, read upwards, and 'long garment' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped wrap worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Crease new fabric

parts.note: a crease is a line in a surface

explanation.surface: A creased piece of newly bought cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a cloth woven from flax.

clue.text: Set up employment structure

parts.note: to frame someone is to set them up
work is employment

explanation.surface: Establishing a system of employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework is a supporting skeleton or underlying system.

clue.text: Departs before inspector is unravelling accounts

indicators.note: before means the departs letter comes first

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: unravelling means coming apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective leaves just as an inspector's case falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' scrambles INSPECTOR IS into ESCRIPTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a description or report of events.
